result.summary:
RESULT: B1, F1, F3 and F6 are fixed with the lines named by the reviewer, and tools/README.md was re-read against the finished page and the fixed server. No tests were written. Nothing was done for F2, F4, F5, F7, F8 (ruled out) and F9-F13 (not requested); see result.issues. Node: the permission system did NOT refuse; the Homebrew binaries are still not executable (stat: -rw-------, ctime 2026-10-01 17:50:35 and 17:53:29 local), so every Node command ran under the private Node 22.21.1 copy (scratchpad/bd/nodebin, the same kind of copy the reviewer used) first in PATH; nothing under <каталог Homebrew> was touched.

B1 (blocking, Q10): the server died of an unhandled EPIPE once the reader of its stdout or stderr was gone. Fix: tools/src/pixel-office/main.js:296-317 (the entry-point block; the listeners are at :303-:305), before main() runs: for (const stream of [process.stdout, process.stderr]) stream.on("error", () => {}). It covers the link line (main.js), every warning of server.js (warn) and journal.js (defaultWarn), and the error messages of main; what cannot be delivered is dropped. In-process callers that pass their own io are not affected. Evidence: (1) before the fix, the reviewer's t16b printed 'answered 500; server: {"c":1,"s":null}; uncaught log: uncaughtException: EPIPE write write EPIPE' and t16 'server alive=false exit={"c":1}' for both cases (reproduced on the unfixed code first); (2) after: t16b 'answered 404; server: "still running"; uncaught log: (none)'; t16 'reader of stderr gone ... status=200 server alive=true' and 'reader of stdout+stderr gone ... status=200 server alive=true'. Because F1 removed the long-name trigger, B1 itself was re-proved with a corrupt journal line, which writes a warning to the closed pipe: (3) the reviewer's literal shell repro (main.js ... 2>&1 | head -n 1 > link, in the background): link line printed, long-name GET 404, GET /api/events?after=0 after a corrupt journal line 200, again 200, process alive; (4) own cases, each with a corrupt line, a long name, /nope and /api/events/ requested and then GET /api/events?after=0&limit=0 = 200 and SIGTERM = exit 0 (for the last, piped case only 'alive, 200': its server was stopped by pid): stdout reader destroyed before the link line (stderr then holds only the corrupt-line warning text, no stack, no EPIPE, no "Unhandled 'error' event"); stderr reader destroyed at start; both; both destroyed after the link line; fd 1 closed with >&-; fd 2 closed with 2>&-; both closed; piped to head -n 1.

F1 (LOW, Q10): server.js:58 STATIC_NAME is now /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/ (at most 64 characters); server.js:66 NO_SUCH_FILE = ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EISDIR, ENAMETOOLONG, ELOOP -> 404 (the old list of three at the former :158-163 is replaced by readPublicFile, :118, used by handleStatic at :189). Evidence: GET /<300 chars>.js 404 {"error":"not_found"} with no stderr line; names of 65, 100, 255, 300 and 5000 characters 404; a real 64-character file is served (200) and a real 65-character file is 404; the reviewer's fuzz t12 (21,600 requests) 0 responses of 5xx (was 78) and server stderr empty.

F3 (LOW, the class of the chmod incident): no link is followed or chmod-ed through any more at the four places and their siblings. state-dir.js: READ_FLAGS (:28) = O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK; withSmallFile (:113) opens, fstat-checks (regular file, at most 4096 bytes) and closes; readSmall (:132) and so readStateText/readSecret (the hook and the server) refuse a link (ELOOP) and cannot block on a pipe; readExistingSecret (:214, the reviewer's :181-208) reads and narrows 0644 -> 0600 with fchmodSync(fd) on the descriptor it checked, never chmodSync(path), and a link is E_STATE_DIR '... (ELOOP)'; writeSmallFile (:262, the reviewer's :232-240) removes whatever stands at <file>.tmp-<pid> (a leftover or a planted link, itself, never followed), creates it with "wx" 0600, sets the mode with fchmodSync(fd), writes all bytes (writeAll) and renames (a link at <file> is replaced by the rename, not followed); ensureSecret writes through writeAll. journal.js: APPEND_FLAGS (:36, the reviewer's :56) = O_RDWR | O_APPEND | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW; READ_FLAGS (:38) for the two read paths (:159, :234); refresh (:202) uses lstat, so a link is JournalReadError ELOOP; starts() reads through readRegularText (:100: lstat, open with READ_FLAGS, fstat, read from the descriptor); notRegular returns ELOOP for a link. server.js: readPublicFile (:118, the reviewer's :157) opens with O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK and checks fstat().isFile(); a link, directory, FIFO or dangling link is 404. Evidence (t-f3, link targets are plain scratch text files or directories, never a binary): write-secret as a link to a 0644 file: ensureSecret throws E_STATE_DIR '(ELOOP)', main exits 1, target mode 0644 and content untouched, hook-side readSecret null; events.jsonl as a link: start refused (exit 1, '(ELOOP)'), read/lineCount/append refuse, target stays empty; events.jsonl turned into a link while the server runs: GET 500 read_failed, POST 500 write_failed, target untouched, recovers when the link is removed; server-starts.jsonl as a link: start refused, starts() throws ELOOP; port and node-path as links: replaced by regular 0600 files, targets untouched; a valid and a dangling link planted at port.tmp-<pid>: removed, never followed, targets untouched, a directory there gives E_STATE_WRITE; public/: links to a file or a directory, a dangling link, a directory x.js, a dotfile, a FIFO (no hang) all 404, the 13 real files byte-identical with the right types and CSP on HTML only. Left as it was on purpose: ensureStateDir chmodSync(dir) (state-dir.js:100) runs only after lstat said 'directory, not a link, own uid'; an fd-based fchmod would fail on a directory the owner cannot open (mode 0000), which today is repaired (observed by the reviewer in his attack 7), and the race needs write access to the parent directory.

F6 (LOW): server.js:248 drainTimeoutSet (a WeakSet) and :254-:261 answerTooLarge: the 5 s idle timeout is set once per socket instead of one more 'timeout' listener per 413. Evidence: the reviewer's t9: '413 on the same connection: 40 of 40; socket still open: true; server stderr: ""; server alive afterwards: true'; the same with 200 requests: 200 of 200, stderr "", alive (before the fix MaxListenersExceededWarning appeared at the 11th).

All 12 grep -F strings of design 9.4 are found (## Pixel Office 1, npm run pixel-office 3, ~/.sai-pixel-office/ 2, the two code.claude.com links 1 each, ### Ограничения 1, остаться «в работе» 1, учётная запись 1, одной вписанной строки 1, навсегда 1, ## Проверка 1, npm run check 2), the only link with a port is http://127.0.0.1:4780, prettier --check clean.

issues.title: Reviewer findings not fixed, with my position
issues.detail: F2 (replay inside the 60 s window), F4 (probe trusts the app marker), F5 (blind cross-site requests), F7 (uncapped ?after=0), F8 (/bin/sh + args assumption): ruled out by ORCH; I do not disagree. F2 and F7 are each about 15 lines if ORCH changes its mind (F2: Map of accepted signatures pruned after 120 s in server.js processBody; F7: a cap on events per response, the page already continues from entries.length). F4's alternative fix, a README known limit, was not added because F4 is on the do-not-fix list. F9 (hook.sh blocks on a FIFO node-path: [ -f ] before the read), F10 (two Host headers), F11 (journal mode not narrowed; only its documentation half, the populated directory, is in the README), F12 (process: pin the handler JSON in ST-01) and F13 (backslash in the project path) were neither requested nor ruled out: not done; F9 is the only one I would still recommend, because it is a one-line change to the code that runs in every session (Q10), with the precondition of write access to the owner's 0700 directory.

issues.title: What the new behaviour means for the tests
issues.detail: (1) B1: the long-name request no longer writes a stderr line (F1), so the test of the reviewer's item (1) needs another warning trigger, for example a corrupt line appended to events.jsonl followed by GET /api/events?after=0 (as the reviewer's t16 does); the process must stay alive and GET /api/events?after=0&limit=0 must answer 200; second test: stdout destroyed before the link line, SIGTERM exit 0, no "Unhandled 'error' event" on stderr. (2) F1: SV-36 gets '/' + 'a'*300 + '.js' -> 404 {"error":"not_found"} and an empty stderr; names up to 64 characters are served, 65 and more are 404. (3) F3: messages are StateDirError E_STATE_DIR 'Файл секрета <path> не читается или не годится (ELOOP)...' for a linked write-secret, JournalReadError/JournalWriteError code 'ELOOP' ('Не удалось прочитать/дописать файл events.jsonl (ELOOP)') for linked events.jsonl and server-starts.jsonl; readSecret and readStateText return null for a link; the link target of such a test must be a plain scratch text file, the target's mode and content must be unchanged. (4) F6: 40 requests of 413 on one connection leave stderr empty (no MaxListenersExceededWarning). (5) The reviewer's t4-state.mjs block 4c assumed that the server starts with linked state files and aborts now; its static block expects 404 for a linked public file, which now holds.

issues.title: Three places where the design text is now narrower than the code
issues.detail: (a) Design 7.2 T8 and T12 speak of a flat public/ and a state directory that is not a link; the code now also refuses a link in place of a state file (secret, events.jsonl, server-starts.jsonl), never follows a link in public/, and replaces a link at port and node-path. (b) The class list of 8.4/AP-014 names fs, net, http, child_process and crypto; the stdio streams of the process (EPIPE on stdout/stderr) belong to it (the reviewer's proposal P1). (c) Design 5.2 says names that do not fit give 404; the bound is now 64 characters.

issues.severity: LOW (left as it was, reason given)
issues.title: ensureStateDir still narrows the directory by path
issues.detail: state-dir.js:100 chmodSync(dir, 0o700) runs only after lstat reported a plain directory of the current user, so it never goes through a link at that moment; making it descriptor-based would stop repairing a directory with mode 0000 (the reviewer observed that repair in his attack 7) and the remaining race needs write access to the parent directory, which has the same power as the owner. Say if ORCH wants the descriptor variant with a path fallback for EACCES.
